core_obligations: Order the local subrings of K by domination, check that the union of a totally ordered collection is again a local subring dominating the members, and apply Zorn's lemma to obtain a maximal one (proof lines 11974-11981).

Show maximality forces the fraction field to be K: otherwise pick t outside it and, according to whether t is transcendental or algebraic, adjoin either t localised at the appropriate prime or a finite extension generated by a multiple of t, producing a strictly larger local subring that dominates (proof lines 11983-11996).
proof_roadmap: Get a maximal local subring by Zorn's lemma (proof lines 11973-11981).
Rule out a smaller fraction field by an explicit enlargement (proof lines 11983-11997).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every local subring of a field K is dominated by a valuation ring with fraction field K (statement lines 11966-11971). The proof does not invoke a general existence theorem for valuation rings: it orders local subrings by domination, applies Zorn's lemma after checking that unions of chains remain local subrings dominating their members, and then shows that a maximal element must have fraction field K by exhibiting, for an element outside the fraction field, an explicit strictly larger local subring in the transcendental and in the algebraic case (proof lines 11973-11997). Splitting the enlargement according to the nature of the chosen element is the content. H2.
